scientific_question: Does a modern multimodal framework raise the ceiling over T8, and does the future proposed method improve robustness to low-signal appearance and invalid depth?

private.tune_split: train=970, dev=137; final_test is inaccessible during tuning
private.final_split: retrain on train+dev=1107, evaluate final_test=283 once
private.input: measured intensity + measured depth + depth-validity map

nyuv2.tune_split: fixed train=715, dev=80 drawn only from official train
nyuv2.input: RGB-to-gray appearance proxy + rawDepths + depth-validity map

phase_1_framework_diagnosis.selection_rule: Choose the modern backbone family using dev mIoU, stability across seeds, parameter cost, and failure-case inspection; do not use final_test/test.

training_regimes: deterministic balanced mixture of corruption types and severities
phase_2_robustness_baselines.evaluation_rule: Each fixed checkpoint is evaluated on clean and every corruption/severity. Never retrain a separate model for each test corruption.
phase_2_robustness_baselines.reporting: Clean is evaluated once; each non-clean corruption is evaluated at all three severities. Report per-condition mIoU and drop from that checkpoint's clean score, never only an aggregate.

phase_3_method_development.rule: Add the new module only after phases 1-2 identify the actual failure mode. Tune on private dev and NYUv2 dev only.
required_ablations: module components added one at a time

final_gate.unlock_condition: Architecture, module, optimizer, input resolution, epoch count, seeds, corruption protocol, and checkpoint selection rule are written and frozen.
